scope: model_55_recheck; supplied full current source/tests and explicitly labeled integration diff if present

findings.title: prepare_model_attempt fence does not compare stored input_digest
findings.issue: On reuse the stored record's input_digest is never compared to the new one before raising ModelAttemptAlreadyRecorded, so divergent bodies under the same task_ref+purpose are indistinguishable from identical replays in error reporting/diagnostics. The deny is still fail-closed (any replay is rejected), but the contract's one-use version-bound/identity accounting cannot be audited.
findings.fix: On reuse, load old payload and compare input_digest to the caller's digest; attach both digests to ModelAttemptAlreadyRecorded so divergence is explicit and testable while still denying all replays.

findings.title: ScopedModelClient swallows arbitrary transport exceptions as unknown-outcome, including pre-send local bugs
findings.issue: The generic `except Exception` around `execute_reserved_groups` converts every non-CapabilityDenied failure (including purely local StorageError from response validation, JSON decode, or usage parsing after the response was actually received) into LLMOutcomeUnknown with external_call_attempted=http_attempted. This is correct for genuinely ambiguous outcomes, but deterministic post-receipt validation failures (bad content-type, invalid finish_reason, non-int usage) are conflated with ambiguous unknowns and permanently poison the task fence even though the provider response is fully known and no retry risk exists.
findings.fix: Distinguish deterministic post-receipt validation/storage errors (e.g. a dedicated exception type raised after `response.read` completes) from genuinely ambiguous transport failures; only convert the latter to LLMOutcomeUnknown and keep retry_allowed=False for ambiguous ones.

findings.title: prepare_model_attempt writes unbounded input_digest without validation
findings.issue: input_digest is stored as provided and never checked against the expected 64-hex pattern used elsewhere for job input digests, so a malformed digest could enter durable state and later comparisons (if added) would misbehave.
findings.fix: Validate input_digest matches `[a-f0-9]{64}` before writing, consistent with JobQueue payload checks.

findings.title: usage observer normalization trusts provider-supplied usage subfields without bounds
findings.issue: prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens and completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens are read via chained .get without type/bounds checks; a non-int or negative value would flow into CostCacheRuntime and settlement accounting, potentially corrupting cost attribution.
findings.fix: Validate cached_tokens and reasoning_tokens are ints within the same 0..1000000 bound used for prompt/completion tokens before passing to the observer.

not_verified: prm.capabilities / AuthorizationDecision semantics and reservation abandon_before_transport behavior
prm.storage.policy execute_reserved_groups / settle / set of reservations and grant scope enforcement
PersonalResearchAssistant and service handlers referenced from composition
CostCacheRuntime record/settlement accounting and unknown-pricing handling
Archive context/synthesis transport classes and citation logic
Actual executable test runs; only the supplied test source was read
findings.summary: The supplied modules enforce strict fail-closed scoping: identity-bound endpoints with redirect denial, per-purpose/per-data-class reservations, a durable one-use attempt fence keyed on task_ref+purpose that denies all replays (including divergent bodies and fresh reservations), bounded pre-transport input/history/output sizes, and an explicit unknown-outcome path that sets retry_allowed=False. The cancellation counterexample in tests confirms StateConflict with no result_ref and retained charge, and composition/queue/worker paths route nested calls through task_context. Remaining gaps are non-P0: input_digest is stored but never compared on fence reuse, generic exception handling conflates deterministic post-receipt validation failures with genuinely ambiguous unknown outcomes (both are safely denied but only one truly risks a replay), and usage subfields lack type/bounds validation before cost accounting. None of these can turn a denial into an allow or cross provider/purpose boundaries, but they weaken auditability and accounting precision, so FIX_P1_FIRST.
